1.pericope_label: God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods

debates.q: Who are the gods among whom God judges?

sides.view: Men delegated with office from God, whose vicegerents naturally bear his name
Possibly angels — one version renders the assembly so, and the Targum reads the righteous
Not angels: the word is nowhere used of them in the Old Testament
Not the gods of the Gentiles, nor idols, nor any creature except men
At the reform of the courts under a king who used nearly these words to his judges
That reign or a later one; two proposals are reported without decision
By Asaph, David’s contemporary; nothing tells against the inscription

outliers.view: Explains the divine presence in court from the English King’s Bench, where the king is always supposed present though he seldom attends
Applies the psalm to village squires and country magistrates, some of whom he says need to go back to school to Asaph

3.pericope_label: Defend the poor and fatherless: do justice to the afflicted and needy

debates.q: Is the judges’ ignorance a defect or a choice?

sides.view: Both — they do not know the law and do not wish to be instructed
A choice: they let themselves walk in darkness, the verb implying inclination
Wilful, and persisted in as their constant course
They know neither God, nor themselves, nor their duty

debates.q: What follows when the foundations are out of course?

sides.view: Every civil institution totters, and even religion loses its influence
Total anarchy and the dissolution of society, like an earthquake
The corruption descends from the supreme rulers to their officers

outliers.view: Interrupts the exposition to praise the judges of his own country as learned, righteous and impartial, and dates the compliment
Names a famous chancellor to show that moral blindness can darken the men of keenest intellectual light

6.pericope_label: I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High

debates.q: In what sense are the judges gods?

sides.view: By commission; the Targum makes them accounted as angels, but magistrates are meant
Like God, by similitude — representatives clothed with his authority
By a title God himself gave them in the law
By an office and honoured name that comes from God, and now brings a doom with it

debates.q: Against whom is the closing prayer directed?

sides.view: Foreign rulers oppressing the community
That inference is erroneous — Israel too, acting untheocratically, is a nation like the nations
It looks forward instead, to the calling of the Gentiles
It is the church addressing Christ against the corruption of the world

outliers.view: Records that the emperor opened the first general council with this verse, to remind the bishops that high office should lift them above party feeling
Reads the death threatened as judicial rather than natural — not a fall into the grave in course of time but an execution
